This is a modern picture of the Aken Cathedral built in 1790. You can see the amount of attention and care put into its architecture, with every inch beautifully constructed. Everyone who worked on it was dedicated to achieving the same vision. This cathedral is still impressive today, no different from when it was first built.

No one said this cathedral was built by aliens or Atlanteans. The idea that Egyptians couldn't build the pyramids without alien help is a racist comment. Charlemagne, the first Holy Roman Emperor, is buried inside this cathedral, but no one claims it to be a tomb; it's recognized as a church. Just like how the pyramids were a temple to their gods, the cathedrals serve as places of worship and spiritual reflection.

Inside, the church remains beautiful, and you can visit Germany to see for yourself. Back then, they believed that every task was an act of making a more godly spiritual world. This is akin to the Manhattan project, which aimed to create eternal peace on earth through scientific innovation. The Manhattan project involved 100,000 scientists working tirelessly. Their hard work led to the development of the atomic bomb, which has since prevented larger-scale wars.

This idea of bringing heaven to earth goes back to humanity's beginnings. Go Goblé Teepe, built around 9,600 B.C.E., is considered the world's first temple. These early structures reflect how humans express their faith through art and architecture. The pillars of this temple are particularly impressive, considering the tools available at that time.

The process of building such temples involves a charismatic leader who shares a vision for creating a sacred space. This leader inspires others to work towards this goal. However, when the leader dies, there is often competition among followers to take over. This is because temples hold significant value as centers of religious and economic activity. Control of a temple means receiving gifts and tributes from visitors.

In summary, the idea of bringing heaven to earth through architecture and science has been a consistent theme throughout human history.
